name: 03-severe-infection
title: Severe infection (severity 3)
question:
Under a severe infection (severity 3), does the SBML extraction track the
BioGears engine's collapse sequence run-for-run, and how large is the known
timing divergence (the extraction report saw the severe course lag by ~8-10 h
against the paper)?
hypothesis:
Both sides follow the same qualitative collapse — capillary leak, compensation,
then hyperdynamic decompensation — but the SBML extraction lags the engine by
several hours on the hypotension milestones, attributable to processes the
extraction does not translate (urine, fever vasodilation, lactate,
intracellular water).
objective:
Run severity 3 on both engines over 48 h, align observables, and quantify the
divergence: SBP<100 and MAP<65 crossing times, SVR-vs-baseline minimum, and the
magnitude of the timing lag — the run-for-run comparison the extraction report
could not do.

expected_behavior.name: severe-collapse-sequence-matches
expected_behavior.observable: SBP, MAP, HR, SVR, tissue_integrity, blood_pathogen
expected_behavior.condition: same timing-shifted collapse with matched inflammation, but a divergent hemodynamic mechanism (engine SVR min 0.952 vs extraction 0.715: the extraction over-shoots vasodilation)
expected_behavior.rationale:
Report: the Antimony model reproduces the severe sequence (capillary leak →
compensation → sympathetic-fatigue decompensation). Run-for-run, the
collapse occurs on both sides (shifted ~11 h) with matched inflammation, but
the hemodynamic mechanism differs: the engine barely vasodilates while the
extraction over-dilates, so the sequence match is partial, not mechanistic.

expected_behavior.name: severe-timing-divergence-quantified
expected_behavior.observable: SBP<100 crossing time (engine vs SBML), MAP<65, SVR ratio
expected_behavior.condition: divergence measured and mechanistically attributed (report: SBML SBP<100 ~37.5 h vs engine ~26-30 h; MAP<65 reached by engine ~45 h, not reached by SBML at 48 h; SVR min ~60% engine vs ~72% SBML)
expected_behavior.rationale:
This is the headline result: the ~8-10 h lag measured run-for-run against
the real engine rather than against the paper milestones.

claim:
Run-for-run, the SBML extraction reproduces BioGears' severe-sepsis inflammation
almost exactly (tissue integrity 0.325/0.325, peak pathogen 60.5/60.6; values at the 48 h horizon, the severe course not yet at its true peak/min) but its
hemodynamic collapse arrives ~11 h LATE: SBP crosses 100 mmHg at 37.5 h in the
extraction vs 26.6 h in the real engine (a 10.9 h lag), with the same ~11 h lag
on the HR>90 compensation. This is the engine-vs-extraction comparison the
extraction report could not make; it confirms and slightly exceeds its ~8-10 h
estimate against the paper.

findings.summary: Severe hemodynamic collapse lags the real engine by ~11 h (SBP<100: 37.5 h vs 26.6 h).
findings.detail:
Both arms, severity 3, 48 h, infection at t=0, run-for-run:
- SBP < 100 mmHg: engine 26.55 h, extraction 37.47 h -> +10.9 h lag.
- HR > 90 /min: engine 26.77 h, extraction 37.55 h -> +10.8 h lag.
- MAP < 65 mmHg: neither crossed (sustained) by 48 h.
- SVR ratio minimum: engine 0.952, extraction 0.715 — the extraction
  over-shoots the vasodilation.
The delay most likely comes from processes the extraction does not translate
(urine loss, fever-driven skin vasodilation, lactate, intracellular water).

findings.summary: The inflammation / pathogen core matches the engine almost bit-for-bit.
findings.detail:
tissue_integrity minimum 0.3248 (engine) vs 0.3248 (extraction); peak
blood_pathogen 60.55 vs 60.60 (both are 48 h-horizon values; *_h = 48.0, so the true peak/min is not yet reached). The Acute Inflammatory Response the extraction
copied from BioGears reproduces the engine's dynamics to ~1e-4 for tissue integrity (~1e-3 for peak pathogen); divergence is
confined to the hemodynamic response, not the inflammation model.

baseline.name: engine-severe
baseline.note: Real BioGears 8.2.0 engine, severity 3, 48 h. SBP<100 at 26.6 h; tissue integrity min 0.325.

variants.name: sbml-severe
variants.note: SBML extraction via viva-tellurium, severity 3, 48 h. SBP<100 at 37.5 h (~11 h late); tissue integrity min 0.325.

severe-collapse-sequence-matches.detail: Same qualitative collapse sequence on both sides, but a qualified match: the vasodilation mechanism diverges (SVR min 0.952 engine vs 0.715 SBML) and the timing lags ~11 h.
